meta.name: Assertion Radar — line-item scenarios
meta.description: Assertion-based audit training scenarios: identify relevant and risky assertions per line item, then match procedures. For the 'Audit Trail' training game suite.
meta.gameplay: Each round: (1) player flags relevant assertions for the line item, (2) flags which are HIGH RISK given the client context, (3) matches procedures to the assertions they test. Trap procedures look correct but address the wrong assertion for the flagged risk.

fields.client_context: the facts that drive assertion risk
fields.assertions_relevant: assertions that are relevant for this line item
fields.assertions_high_risk: map of assertion -> why the context makes it risky
fields.procedures: list of {procedure, tests[], trap, trap_explanation, isa_ref}
fields.isa_refs: ISA references for the overall scenario

scenarios.client_context: New online sales channel launched in March. Sales managers' bonuses are tied to monthly sales targets. Year-end falls in the peak holiday season.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Bonus pressure plus a new channel creates incentive to book fictitious or prematurely recognized sales.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Holiday peak season concentrates transactions around the period boundary.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: New channel may have untested pricing, discount and returns logic.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of online sales invoices to shipping documents and customer payment receipts
Trace a sample of December shipping documents to the sales ledger in January and vice versa
Perform analytical review comparing gross margin percentage by channel month-on-month
Confirm year-end receivable balances with customers directly
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirmation tests balance-sheet assertions on receivables, not the revenue occurrence or cut-off risk flagged by the context.

procedures.procedure: Review the returns provision calculation after year-end and compare to historical return rates

scenarios.client_context: Revenue on construction contracts is recognized over time using percentage of completion based on costs incurred to date. Several large projects span multiple years.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Percentage-of-completion depends on reliable cost estimates and total project cost forecasts — a high-judgment estimate.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Recognizing revenue ahead of actual progress inflates current-year results.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Costs incurred but not yet invoiced or recorded must be captured in the stage-of-completion measure.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the percentage of completion using independently verified cost-to-date figures and compare with management's
Compare recorded costs-to-date with the project engineer's site progress reports and photos
Review the change-order log for approved variations not yet reflected in total contract value
Physically inspect completed buildings at the client's head office
procedures.trap_explanation: Physical inspection of finished buildings tests existence of assets, not the revenue recognition estimate at risk here.

procedures.procedure: Enquire of the project manager about expected losses on loss-making contracts and review the calculation

scenarios.client_context: Annual subscription software contracts billed upfront, revenue recognized ratably over the subscription term. Customer base grew 60% this year; churn is rising.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Ratable recognition requires a reliable contract-start and term data pipeline — fast growth may outpace the billing system's controls.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Upfront billing creates incentive to book renewals or extensions early.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Upfront billing must sit in contract liabilities, not revenue — misclassification risk is high.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the deferred revenue release schedule for a sample of contracts and agree opening balances to prior year
Match the contract liability roll-forward to the billing system's subscription records
Vouch a sample of recognized revenue amounts to the underlying signed contracts and start dates
Send positive confirmations to a sample of customers requesting their view of service periods
procedures.trap_explanation: Customer confirmation of balances tests receivables assertions; it does not test the ratable recognition accuracy risk.

scenarios.client_context: Other income includes government grants for energy-saving equipment, scrap sales, and a one-off gain on disposal of a machine. The line tripled versus prior year.

assertions_high_risk.classification: A tripling suggests items may be misclassified — operating items could be hidden here or gains parked outside core revenue.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: One-off disposal gains can be overstated or fictitious.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Grant recognition timing depends on conditions attached.

procedures.procedure: Agree grant receipts to the grant agreements and test whether recognition conditions were met in the period
Vouch the disposal gain to the sales invoice, de-registration documents and asset register removal
Analytically compare scrap sales volume to production output
Inspect the machine physically at the buyer's premises
procedures.trap_explanation: The machine is sold — physical inspection is impossible and irrelevant; the disposal documentation is the evidence.

scenarios.client_context: Component prices fell sharply mid-year. Inventory is measured using weighted average cost. Gross margin improved more than management expected.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Falling input prices make the costing method's application critical — weighted average must be computed on the correct layers.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Goods received near year-end must hit both inventory and cost of sales in the correct period.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the weighted average cost for sample product lines and compare to the ledger
Test the purchase cut-off around year-end using goods-received notes and supplier invoices
Perform analytical review of margin by product line, comparing standard cost to actual
Inspect supplier contracts for volume rebates recorded as income instead of cost reduction

scenarios.client_context: The client employs agency staff through a staffing platform. Payroll is processed in-house. Several new shift managers can approve timesheets.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: New shift managers approving timesheets increases risk of fictitious or ghost employees.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Agency staff costs may be misallocated between payroll and agency fees.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Year-end hours worked but paid in January must accrue in the correct period.

procedures.procedure: Match the payroll headcount to HR files and inspect contracts for a sample of employees
Recalculate gross pay for a sample including overtime and shift premiums
Agree accrued year-end hours to the January payroll run
Obtain a bank confirmation for the payroll account
procedures.trap_explanation: Bank confirmation verifies cash existence, not whether recorded payroll expense is genuine and complete.

scenarios.client_context: Fleet of trucks depreciated over 5 years straight-line. This year, 20 new electric trucks were added, and the useful life of diesel trucks was extended from 5 to 8 years due to slower replacement cycle.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The change in useful life is a change in estimate applied prospectively — prospective application and arithmetic must be verified.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: New trucks must be depreciated from the in-service date, not the purchase order date.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate depreciation for a sample of assets, re-performing the revised life calculation
Agree new truck additions to registration documents and in-service dates
Review the basis for the life extension: maintenance records, technical assessments, replacement plans
Physically inspect a sample of trucks at the depot
procedures.trap_explanation: Truck existence is a balance-sheet concern; the expense risk here is the estimate change, which inspection cannot verify.

scenarios.client_context: The client refinanced all borrowings mid-year to a variable-rate facility. Interest is accrued monthly; loan arrangement fees were paid and capitalized.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Variable-rate interest requires correct rate and day-count application across two different facilities in one year.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Accrued interest at year-end on the new facility must be captured; arrangement fee amortization must be complete.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate interest using the facility agreements, rate confirmations and outstanding balances
Agree interest payments per the bank statements to the loan schedule and test the year-end accrual
Reperform the amortization of capitalized arrangement fees over the facility term
Obtain bank confirmation of loan balances at year-end
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirmation of the loan principal addresses balance assertions; it does not test whether the expense is accurately and completely recorded.

scenarios.client_context: High cash turnover from daily restaurant receipts. Three bank accounts, one recently opened for a new location. Cash is physically counted weekly by shift leads.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Cash is the most deferrable asset — weekly counts by shift leads (not independent) increase misappropriation risk.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: A recently opened account could be omitted from the general ledger mapping or the reconciliation process.

procedures.procedure: Obtain bank confirmations for all accounts, including those with nil or closed during the year, from the bank directly
Test the bank reconciliations for each account for the final three months, tracing outstanding items to subsequent clearing
Count physical cash on hand at year-end surprise and compare with the ledger
Review the bank resolution for authorized signatories and pledge/collateral disclosures
Analytically review weekly cash counts vs daily POS reports

scenarios.client_context: Two large customers account for 45% of receivables. The allowance is a single pooled percentage based on age. One large customer was 120 days overdue at year-end.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A pooled age-based allowance may not reflect the specific 120-day overdue customer — ECL must reflect individual evidence.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Concentration plus possible fictitious balances to mask misappropriation.

procedures.procedure: Send direct positive confirmations to a spread of customers including the two largest and the overdue one
Test subsequent cash receipt of the overdue balance after year-end
Recalculate the ECL provision using the matrix and assess whether individual impairments are required for the overdue customer
Trace credit notes issued after year-end to the year-end balance
Physically count the receivables ledger printout at the client's office
procedures.trap_explanation: Receivables are not physical assets — a ledger printout is a document, not the balance itself; existence is tested via confirmation and subsequent receipt.

scenarios.client_context: Fast-moving electronics inventory at three warehouses. The year-end count instructions were issued late; two warehouses use third-party logistics providers who perform their own counts.

assertions_high_risk.existence: 3PL warehouses mean the client's staff did not perform the count — auditor attendance or alternative evidence is needed.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Electronics obsolesce fast — NRV testing and slow-moving analysis is critical.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Late count instructions raise the risk of uncounted goods in transit and consignment stock.

procedures.procedure: Attend the physical count at one own warehouse and obtain 3PL count reports plus direct confirmation of 3PL-held stock
Perform NRV testing on slow-moving lines comparing selling price to cost, using post-year-end sales data
Test cut-off: last dispatch/receipt documents before and after count date traced to ledger
Review consignment agreements to ensure consigned-in goods are excluded and consigned-out goods included
Confirm receivable balances with customers to verify inventory sales
procedures.trap_explanation: Receivables confirmation tests receivables, not inventory existence; the correct evidence is count attendance and 3PL confirmation.

scenarios.client_context: Livestock (dairy cattle) measured at fair value less costs to sell per IAS 41. Herd sizes are tracked in an animal register; a disease outbreak occurred in the region mid-year.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Disease outbreak creates risk that animals recorded have died or been culled without the register being updated.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Fair value of livestock is volatile and outbreak-affected — expert evidence needed.

procedures.procedure: Observe the herd count using ear tags and reconcile to the animal register
Evaluate the work of an agricultural valuation expert and test key inputs to market price data
Inspect veterinary and insurance records for deaths and culls around year-end
Vouch the cost-to-sell deduction to transporter and market fee invoices

scenarios.client_context: A major plant extension was completed mid-year, constructed partly by the client's own staff. Several older machines were idle at year-end and held for sale discussions started.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Own-construction costs must be correctly capitalized (materials, labor, overhead) without internally generated profit; idle machines trigger impairment and held-for-sale classification review.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Self-built asset costs may be expensed rather than capitalized.

procedures.procedure: Vouch capitalized own-construction costs to timesheets, material invoices and overhead allocation calculations
Physically inspect the plant extension and trace selected machines to the fixed asset register
Assess the idle machines for impairment indicators and review management's recoverable amount calculations
Inspect title deeds and check for encumbrances/mortgages on the plant
Review repair and maintenance expense for items wrongly expensed that should be capital replacements

scenarios.client_context: Office portfolio at fair value using external valuers. The market softened this year; one building was reclassified to owner-occupied after the tenant (a group company) expanded into it.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Soft market makes fair value estimates more judgmental; reclassification date and measurement basis switch must be correct.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Reclassification must be disclosed; owner-occupied means IAS 16 measurement, not IAS 40.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the external valuers' competence, objectivity and methodology; test key assumptions (yields, rents) to market data
Physically inspect a sample of properties and confirm occupancy
Inspect title documents and land registry extracts for ownership and encumbrances
Review the reclassification documentation and verify measurement at transition and disclosure

scenarios.client_context: Goodwill arose from a takeover two years ago. The acquired chain's like-for-like sales have declined for six consecutive quarters. Management tests goodwill at the group level, not per cash-generating unit.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Sustained decline is a clear impairment indicator; testing at group level rather than CGU level can mask impairment of the acquired chain.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Goodwill must only remain if the acquisition actually occurred and generated it.

procedures.procedure: Review management's CGU identification against how the business is managed and the acquisition's synergies
Reperform the impairment test for the acquired chain CGU, challenging cash flow forecasts against the six-quarter decline
Vouch the original purchase price allocation and headroom recorded at acquisition
Confirm the goodwill balance with the previous auditors
procedures.trap_explanation: Goodwill is not confirmable with a third party; existence is tested via the acquisition documentation and PPA.

scenarios.client_context: Development costs on a new drug capitalized after reaching technical feasibility. Costs include clinical trial spend. A competitor launched an equivalent drug this year.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Competitor launch is an impairment indicator; amortization period assumptions need revisiting.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Capitalized trial costs must relate to actual, traceable trial activity.

procedures.procedure: Vouch capitalized clinical trial costs to trial contracts, invoices and progress reports
Review the technical feasibility documentation and timing of capitalization start
Assess impairment indicators from the competitor launch and reperform the recoverable amount test
Discuss the development pipeline with the R&D director and document the drug's approval status

scenarios.client_context: The client runs a JIT purchasing operation with over 200 suppliers. Purchasing, goods receipt and invoice matching are handled in three different systems that are not fully integrated. Several suppliers accept payment 90 days after invoice, and the finance team records payables only when the invoice is entered, not when goods are received.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Unrecorded liabilities for goods received but not yet invoiced (GRNI) are the classic payables risk; the unintegrated systems make it worse.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Duplicate or fictitious supplier accounts could cause payables to be overstated or used to route fraudulent payments.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Year-end goods receipts straddling the reporting date may be recorded in the wrong period.

procedures.procedure: Search the unmatched goods-received report after year-end and trace receipts to the payables ledger and subsequent payments
Examine a sample of post-year-end supplier invoices and identify any that relate to goods or services received before year-end
Vouch a sample of recorded payables balances to supplier invoices and goods-received notes
Review supplier statements received after year-end and reconcile any unrecorded items
Confirm year-end balances directly with the three largest customers
procedures.trap_explanation: This tests receivables, not payables. The direction of the test is wrong: confirming customers verifies recorded sales/receivables (occurrence for receivables), while payables completeness requires looking at suppliers.

scenarios.client_context: A grocery retailer receives daily deliveries from hundreds of local producers. Many producers send consolidated invoices monthly. At year-end the warehouse log shows significant goods received in the last week of December for which no invoices were received until February.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Monthly consolidated invoicing means large liabilities can sit unrecorded for weeks after delivery.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: High-volume daily deliveries make period-end cut-off errors easy to make and hard to spot.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile the December warehouse receiving log to recorded goods-received-not-invoiced balances
Perform a completeness check by comparing December purchase volumes to the same month of the prior year and investigating outliers
Trace a sample of warehouse receipts in the last week of December to the general ledger to confirm the correct period
Verify that amounts owed to the group's logistics subsidiary are presented separately from trade payables

scenarios.client_context: The client accrues monthly for cloud hosting and digital advertising based on a standard monthly estimate. In December it ran an unusually large year-end campaign through an agency that only invoices in arrears, and the accrual was not updated for the campaign.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Estimates-based accruals are easy to understate when actual activity spikes outside the normal pattern.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Standard monthly accrual rates may no longer reflect contracted prices after vendor renegotiation.

procedures.procedure: Compare the December accrual to the invoices actually received in January and February and assess the accuracy of the estimate
Recalculate the cloud accrual using the revised contract rates in the current vendor agreements
Review the accrual roll-back reconciliation and investigate significant differences
Observe the year-end physical count of advertising materials in the warehouse
procedures.trap_explanation: Observing a physical inventory count tests the existence of physical assets, not whether service accruals are complete and accurate. The procedure doesn't touch the assertion at risk.

scenarios.client_context: A group of patients has filed a class action claiming a defect in a hip implant. Legal counsel estimates a probable outflow between EUR 8m and EUR 15m. Management recognised EUR 8m, the bottom of the range, arguing the low end is 'more likely'. The claim is not disclosed in the notes.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Management chose the bottom of counsel's range without support; provisions require the best estimate of the outflow.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Non-disclosure of the nature and expected timing of the claim breaches IAS 37 disclosure requirements.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: There may be other smaller claims not yet routed through legal.

procedures.procedure: Obtain and evaluate the written response of external legal counsel on the probability and estimated range of the outflow
Review management's basis for selecting EUR 8m and challenge it against counsel's analysis of the most likely outcome
Inspect board minutes and correspondence with regulators to identify any further product claims not recorded
Review the draft financial statements to confirm the claim's nature, expected timing and uncertainty are disclosed
Vouch the recorded provision to the invoice received from the law firm for legal fees
procedures.trap_explanation: The law firm's fee invoice relates to legal costs expense, not the amount of the product liability. Vouching it does not evaluate whether EUR 8m is the best estimate of the claim's outflow.

scenarios.client_context: The client sells extended two-year warranties on its devices. The provision is calculated by applying a warranty-claim rate derived from three years of historical data. This year the client launched a new product line with an unproven battery supplier, and early consumer reports mention overheating. The historical claim rate was not adjusted.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A historical claim rate may not predict claims for a new product with a known defect signal; the estimate is likely understated.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Claims arising in the last weeks of the year may not yet be logged in the claims database.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the provision by re-deriving the expected claim rate per product line from current claims data
Compare the claims rate of the new battery-powered line with the rest of the portfolio and challenge management's assumption
Review post-year-end customer returns and warranty claims for items affecting the current year provision
Confirm the provision balance with the external warranty service provider
procedures.trap_explanation: The provision is an internally generated estimate, not a balance owed to the service provider. Confirmation gives no evidence about whether the claim-rate estimate is reasonable; an auditor must test the estimate itself.

scenarios.client_context: The client leases 120 stores under IFRS 16. During the year it renegotiated 20 leases, some with variable payments linked to sales. Several leases contain renewal options that management has not assessed, and two stores are scheduled to close early next year.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Renegotiated leases and short-term handshake agreements may not all be captured in the IFRS 16 sub-ledger.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Variable payments and lease-term reassessments for the two closing stores directly affect depreciation and impairment.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: The client must have the contractual right to use the assets for the recognized lease term.

procedures.procedure: Select a sample of signed lease contracts and agree the right-of-use amount to the lease liability schedule and discount rate used
Inspect a sample of lease agreements to confirm renewal options were evaluated and the lease term is supportable
Perform a completeness sweep of rent payments in the cash book and trace them to recognized lease contracts
Assess the impairment of right-of-use assets for the two stores identified for closure

scenarios.client_context: The client operates a leased fleet of trucks and warehouses. For a group of new leases, management used the incremental borrowing rate from a five-year-old policy document. Two leases have rent indexed to inflation and one contains a purchase option the client expects to exercise, but neither is reflected in the liability.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The discount rate and lease-term assumptions (indexation, purchase option) drive the liability measurement; outdated assumptions understate it.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Short-term warehouse rentals arranged by local depot managers may never reach head office.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the liability for a sample of leases and evaluate the source and currency-term of the discount rate used
Inspect lease agreements for indexation clauses and purchase options and verify these are included in the measurement
Review the interest expense and current/non-current split of lease liabilities for accuracy and disclosure
Inspect the titles deeds of the trucks to verify the client's legal ownership
procedures.trap_explanation: Leased trucks are not owned by the client, so title deeds won't exist; and even if they did, this tests ownership of PPE, not the measurement of lease liabilities. It misses the actual risk.

scenarios.client_context: The client funds a large residential project with a syndicated development facility that includes a covenant requiring pre-sold units to exceed 60%. Halfway through the year the covenant was breached and the bank granted a waiver valid only until next June. The facility is classified entirely as non-current.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The covenant breach and waiver must be disclosed; it may also trigger going-concern considerations.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Without the waiver the facility may be repayable on demand, requiring current classification.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Interest and arrangement fees on drawdowns may not all be accrued.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the loan agreement and the bank's waiver letter and confirm the breach and waiver are disclosed in the notes
Confirm the year-end balance, terms and covenant status directly with the syndicate's agent bank
Assess whether the classification as non-current remains appropriate given the waiver's expiry before the next reporting date
Recalculate accrued interest on each drawdown and vouch arrangement fees to invoices

scenarios.client_context: The client has accumulated losses of EUR 40m and recognised a deferred tax asset on all of them, relying on a five-year forecast that shows profitability from year three. The forecast assumes a licensing deal that has not yet been signed, and the tax asset was not discounted. Losses for part of the group expire within two years.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Recognition depends entirely on whether future taxable profit is probable; an unsigned deal is weak evidence.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The nature and expiry of losses, and the amount of DTA not recognised, must be disclosed.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the reliability of the profit forecast, including the status of the licensing deal and its support in board minutes
Agree the loss carryforwards to filed tax returns and confirm expiry dates with the tax advisor
Review the disclosure of unused losses, expiry dates and the deferred tax asset recognised in the notes
Recalculate the deferred tax asset using the statutory tax rate and verify the effects of indexation are excluded
procedures.trap_explanation: 'Indexation' is not a deferred tax concept — deferred tax is calculated on temporary differences at the enacted tax rate. The procedure is pseudo-technical and tests nothing real.

scenarios.client_context: During the year the client completed a follow-on equity offering, issued new shares to the founders under an employee incentive plan, and bought back a small block of treasury shares. All movements are posted to a single 'equity' account, and issue costs of EUR 2m were expensed.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Posting all equity movements to a single account obscures the required split between share capital, premium, treasury and incentive-plan reserves.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Each class of share movement and the reserve for the incentive plan requires separate disclosure in the statement of changes in equity.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Issue costs should reduce share premium, not run through profit or loss.

procedures.procedure: Vouch share issuances to the prospectus, subscription agreements, cash receipts and the share register maintained by the transfer agent
Trace the movement in each equity component through the statement of changes in equity and agree to the general ledger
Inspect the board and shareholder approvals for the buyback and the incentive plan grant
Reclassify the EUR 2m issue costs from operating expenses to share premium and check treatment against IAS 32

scenarios.client_context: The two shareholder-directors declared and paid themselves quarterly dividends throughout the year, including one large payment just before year-end that emptied the distributable reserve. A further dividend was proposed after year-end and recorded as a liability in the current year accounts.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Payments to shareholder-directors may be remuneration or loans disguised as dividends.
assertions_high_risk.classification: A proposed (not yet declared) dividend is not a liability of the reporting period under IFRS.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Distributing more than distributable reserves can be legally invalid under Dutch law.

procedures.procedure: Vouch each dividend payment to shareholders' resolutions, dividend declarations and bank statements
Agree proposed dividends to the post year-end board minutes and confirm they are disclosed as a subsequent event rather than recognized as a liability
Recalculate distributable reserves from the prior-year audited accounts and cumulative results
Confirm dividend income received from the client's own subsidiary in the group accounts
procedures.trap_explanation: Dividends received from a subsidiary are group income, not relevant to dividends paid by the parent — and in any case it tests income recognition, not the classification/cut-off risk in the item under audit.

scenarios.line_item: Investment fund holdings at fair value (Level 3)
scenarios.client_context: The fund holds private equity and infrastructure stakes valued using the investee managers' unaudited NAV statements. This year, 30% of the portfolio moved from Level 2 to Level 3 after a fund suspended redemptions, and the valuation report from the external expert is dated two months after the reporting date.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Level 3 valuations are highly subjective, especially with stale NAVs and a suspended fund.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The fair value hierarchy transfers and valuation techniques require disclosure under IFRS 13.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the competence, capabilities and objectivity of management's valuation expert
Confirm holdings with the custodian and fund administrators for existence and title
Test the Level 3 model inputs (discount rates, comparables) and challenge the stale NAVs against redemption-suspension evidence
Review the fair value hierarchy disclosure, including the reasons for transfers between levels
Agree purchase prices of the stakes to historical invoices and payment records
procedures.trap_explanation: Historical cost provides no evidence about the year-end fair value of Level 3 instruments. The assertion at risk is valuation, and this procedure tests the wrong measurement basis.

scenarios.line_item: Loans and advances to customers (ECL provision)
scenarios.client_context: A mid-size bank calculates expected credit losses with a model that blends internal ratings and forward-looking macro scenarios. This year the model's overnight reruns became slow, so the risk team manually patched PD values for two segments in a spreadsheet outside the controlled environment. The consumer segment shows rising 30+ days-past-due rates.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Manual spreadsheet patches to a controlled model create both error and override risk in a highly judgemental estimate.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Segments omitted or added late to the model would be missing from the ECL provision.

procedures.procedure: Test the design and operation of controls over the ECL model, including change management and access to the spreadsheet
Reperform the ECL calculation for the two manually patched segments and compare to the model output
Compare the actual 30+ DPD roll rates against the model's assumed transition matrices and assess the impact of emerging deterioration
Confirm the loan balances for a sample of corporate borrowers directly with the borrowers

scenarios.line_item: Receivable from a related party (majority shareholder)
scenarios.client_context: The balance includes EUR 3m due from a holding company owned by the CEO's family. There is no written agreement, no interest, and no repayment schedule. The amount has been outstanding for 18 months and is presented within trade receivables.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: An unsecured, interest-free, long-overdue family receivable may be irrecoverable — impairment assessment is required.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Related party balances and terms require disclosure under IAS 24; hiding it inside trade receivables is misleading.
assertions_high_risk.classification: This is not a trade receivable arising from operations.

procedures.procedure: Identify the related party through ownership records and confirm the terms of the arrangement with management and the counterparty
Assess the recoverability of the receivable, including the counterparty's cash flows and any agreed repayment plan
Review the draft notes for disclosure of the related party relationship, amount, terms and any allowances
Reclassify the balance from trade receivables to other receivables and verify the ageing analysis excludes it from the trade debtor provision calculation

scenarios.line_item: Contingent liabilities (disclosure of a pending regulatory fine)
scenarios.client_context: The environmental regulator has notified the client of a probable fine for a landfill permit breach, but the amount is not yet determinable. Management recorded no provision and made no disclosure, noting that 'the amount is unknown'. Separately, a competitor's claim against the client was dismissed and management still discloses it.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: A probable but unmeasurable outflow is still a contingent liability requiring disclosure — omission leaves the accounts incomplete.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Disclosing a dismissed claim is a false disclosure; contingencies must reflect the current legal position.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the regulator's notification and correspondence with legal counsel to assess probability and estimability of the fine
Review the draft notes to confirm the contingent liability is disclosed with its nature and estimate range where possible
Obtain the court's dismissal order for the competitor claim and confirm the outdated disclosure is removed
Accrue the maximum possible fine amount as a provision in the current year
procedures.trap_explanation: This is not even a valid audit procedure — it is preparing the client's books. It also applies the wrong accounting: a remote or unmeasurable amount is disclosed, not provisioned at a made-up maximum.

scenarios.line_item: Cash and cash equivalents (money market funds and crypto holdings)
scenarios.client_context: The client parks surplus cash in a money market fund and a small amount in a crypto exchange account. The fund suspended redemptions in December due to market stress, and the crypto exchange is unregulated and unaudited. Management classifies everything as 'cash and cash equivalents'.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Balances at an unregulated exchange may not exist at all — the client may only have an unsecured claim.
assertions_high_risk.classification: A suspended MMF no longer meets the definition of cash equivalents and must be reclassified.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Concentration and restriction on access require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Obtain direct confirmation of balances from the MMF and the crypto exchange at the reporting date
Agree MMF units to fund statements and evaluate the redemption suspension's effect on the cash-equivalent classification
Review the bank reconciliations for all accounts and investigate long-outstanding items
Assess whether restricted balances and the crypto concentration are disclosed in the notes

scenarios.line_item: Construction work in progress ( harbour project assets)
scenarios.client_context: The client builds port infrastructure under long-term contracts. Its CWIP includes direct costs and an allocation of overhead, but the site accountants in three countries report monthly via emailed spreadsheets with no standard template. Two projects have stalled because the client's subcontractor is insolvent, and interest on the related project loan continues to be capitalized.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Overhead allocation via emailed non-standard spreadsheets is prone to computational and cut-off errors.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Stalled projects may need impairment testing; capitalizing interest may no longer be appropriate.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Subcontractor invoices arriving late from foreign sites may be missing from CWIP.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of CWIP additions to supplier invoices, subcontractor applications and internal labour records
Review the overhead allocation model and reperform the allocation for one project
Perform site visits and physical inspection of the assets under construction for the stalled projects, and inspect the insolvency notice of the subcontractor
Review post-year-end subcontractor invoices for December work and test the capitalization cut-off
Review whether interest capitalization on the stalled project loans complies with IAS 23's 'interruptions' guidance

scenarios.client_context: The client recognizes subscription revenue ratably over 12-month contracts. This quarter it introduced an annual 'success fee' add-on and started recognizing it upfront at contract signature. Sales staff can create contracts in the CRM with custom start dates, and several deals signed in late December have January start dates backdated to December.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Fictitious or modified CRM contracts could create revenue with no genuine customer.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Backdated start dates pull future-period revenue into the current year.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Upfront recognition of the success fee violates the single performance obligation principle of IFRS 15.

procedures.procedure: Vouch a sample of December contracts to signed agreements and independently verify start dates against CRM audit logs and first billing dates
Evaluate the accounting policy for the success fee against the five-step IFRS 15 model and reperform revenue allocation for a sample
Review the IT general controls over contract creation and modification rights in the CRM
Analytically compare December daily revenue with surrounding months and investigate spikes near month-end
Confirm outstanding subscription balances with a sample of customers at year-end
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirming balances receivable from customers tests receivables existence and sales occurrence, not completeness of revenue. Revenue completeness is better tested with the CRM-to-ledger completeness walk.

scenarios.client_context: The client recognizes revenue using percentage of completion based on costs incurred to date. In December, to hit the annual bonus target, management accelerated recognition on a bridge project using forecast total costs that were revised down without evidence. The contract also includes an unpriced variation being negotiated with the customer.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The estimate of progress and forecast costs directly drives the recognized amount — a management bias hotspot.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Unpriced variations recognized at management's preferred value may overstate the contract asset.

procedures.procedure: Vouch costs incurred on the bridge project to invoices, payroll and subcontractor certifications to verify the input to the progress measure
Evaluate the revision of forecast total costs, including corroboration from the project engineer and quantity surveyor
Inspect correspondence with the customer on the variation and assess whether any value is recognized appropriately
Perform a retrospective review of prior-period estimates for signs of management bias

scenarios.client_context: The client grows and packs fresh produce. Harvest costs are capitalized into inventory until sold. This year an early frost destroyed part of the standing crop, and management expensed all replanting costs to cost of sales in one month, mixing them with normal operating costs. The picking subcontractor's invoices are received in bulk with a two-month lag.

assertions_high_risk.classification: Replanting costs of the next cycle may belong in new biological assets or future harvest inventory, not current cost of sales.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: The two-month invoicing lag means December harvest costs are likely unrecorded at year-end.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: The frost loss may include a one-off write-off that requires separate presentation or disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Accrue and test harvest costs by reconciling pick records and worker timesheets to cost of sales and the accrual balance
Inspect the frost damage assessment and replanting plan and evaluate the classification of the related costs
Review post-year-end subcontractor invoices and allocate costs between harvest periods based on pick dates
Perform analytical procedures comparing cost per kg by farm and month and investigate anomalies around the frost event

scenarios.client_context: The client pays 4,000 agency nurses through a payroll bureau. Turnover is high and the payroll masterfile is maintained by a single HR officer who also has payment approval rights. A few terminated employees remained on the masterfile during the year, and December shift premiums were calculated using an outdated collective agreement.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Ghost employees or payments after termination are likely given the segregation-of-duties failure.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Applying an outdated collective agreement systematically misstates shift premiums.

procedures.procedure: Test the segregation of duties and access rights over the payroll masterfile and payment approval
Match the payroll masterfile to current active staff lists and HR termination records and investigate leavers still paid
Recalculate December shift premiums using the current collective agreement and quantify the difference
Review the pension contribution accrual for December and its allocation between the pension expense and payable

scenarios.client_context: The client stores slow-moving stock at 12 third-party warehouses across Europe and records it based on monthly emailed stock statements from the warehouse operators. One operator is in financial difficulty and has stopped responding to emails; the client's last physical count of that site was two years ago.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Stock recorded from operator emails may no longer be physically present — especially with a distressed operator.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Operators may have pledged or sold the consigned goods; title may be contested.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Slow-moving stock at a distressed site likely needs write-down.

procedures.procedure: Attend or arrange a physical count at the distressed operator's site, or use another auditor's count attendance
Obtain confirmations directly from the warehouse operators of quantities held on the client's behalf
Inspect consignment agreements for title clauses and pledges, and review legal correspondence regarding the distressed operator
Perform ageing analysis and assess NRV write-downs for slow-moving lines, with extra scrutiny on the unresponsive site
Review the client's purchase ledger to confirm no inventory was recorded twice
procedures.trap_explanation: Checking for double-counted purchases tests the accuracy/occurrence of recorded inventory, not completeness. The risk direction here is existence (recorded stock that isn't there), so this procedure misses the point entirely.

scenarios.line_item: Adjusting and non-adjusting events after the reporting period
scenarios.client_context: After year-end but before the accounts were authorized, a volcanic eruption shut down the client's main route for six weeks, and a major customer went bankrupt owing EUR 2m at year-end. Management argues both events arose after the reporting date and made no adjustments or disclosures. The auditor's fieldwork ended a week before the eruption.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The customer's bankruptcy provides evidence about the year-end recoverability of the receivable — an adjusting event requiring an allowance.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The eruption is a non-adjusting event, but its financial effect must still be disclosed.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the customer's insolvency filing and assess whether the year-end receivable required an impairment allowance
Review the subsequent-events procedures performed by management up to the authorization date, including board minutes and cash flow forecasts
Evaluate the impact of the route closure on forecasts and assess whether disclosure of the non-adjusting event is made
Confirm the customer's year-end balance directly with the customer
procedures.trap_explanation: Confirmation at year-end provides no evidence about the customer's post-year-end insolvency. The bankruptcy filing is the relevant evidence — the adjusting-event issue is about conditions arising after year-end, which confirmation cannot address.

scenarios.client_context: The client has negative operating cash flow and depends on closing a Series C funding round two months after year-end. The round is not yet signed; term sheets exist from two investors. Management prepares the accounts on a going-concern basis with only a brief note. Monthly net cash outflow has doubled since mid-year.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Material uncertainty related to going concern must be disclosed in a prominent note; a brief mention is insufficient.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: If the going-concern basis is inappropriate, asset values and classifications (current/non-current) change fundamentally.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate management's cash-flow forecast covering at least 12 months from authorization, testing key assumptions on burn rate and funding timing
Inspect the term sheets and correspondence with investors and assess the likelihood and timing of the funding round
Review the draft disclosure for a material-uncertainty-related-to-going-concern statement and its prominence
Written statement from management that the round will close
procedures.trap_explanation: A bare management representation is not sufficient appropriate evidence for a matter as significant as going concern. It must be corroborated with external evidence (term sheets, investor correspondence) and forecast testing.

scenarios.line_item: Current tax expense and tax payable
scenarios.client_context: The client operates stores in five countries, each with a local finance lead preparing tax computations on local templates. Transfer prices between the stores' procurement entity and national entities were set late in the year. One country's tax return was filed under protest after a dispute over permanent establishment status. The group tax provision is a single consolidated number.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Late-set transfer prices mean some current tax liabilities were only estimated per country.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The PE dispute could create additional tax and penalties in the disputed country.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: A single consolidated provision obscures per-country errors.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate the tax computation for each country and agree the provision components to the local templates and returns
Discuss the PE dispute with the group tax counsel and inspect correspondence with the tax authority to assess additional exposure
Agree amounts paid after year-end to the tax authorities' assessments and final settlement letters
Review the effective tax rate reconciliation and disclosure of uncertain tax positions

scenarios.client_context: The client owns and leases out 40 hotels. During the year it changed the useful life of building improvements from 25 to 40 years, citing 'better build quality', reducing annual depreciation by 30%. Several lease-out contracts were renegotiated to shorter terms, and the change was applied retrospectively without restating comparatives.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The change in useful life is an accounting estimate change that must be applied prospectively; retrospective application misstates comparatives.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The estimate change requires evidence about actual asset condition; 'better build quality' needs support.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate depreciation under the new useful life for a sample of assets and verify prospective application
Inspect engineering reports or expert assessments supporting the revised useful life and challenge management's rationale
Review the disclosure of the nature and effect of the estimate change in the notes
For the buildings, verify ownership through title deeds held by the bank
procedures.trap_explanation: Rights-and-obligations for buildings is a balance-sheet assertion about PPE, not the depreciation expense line under audit. It may be valid PPE work, but it provides no evidence about whether depreciation is accurate.

scenarios.line_item: Interest expense on borrowings and leases
scenarios.client_context: The client capitalizes interest on construction projects and expenses the rest. During the year it hedged variable-rate borrowings with interest rate swaps, and hedge documentation was completed three months after the swap was entered. The finance team also expensed arrangement fees for the new facility in full rather than amortizing.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Late hedge documentation means hedge accounting cannot be applied from inception — swap movements may be misclassified as interest.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Expensing arrangement fees immediately misclassifies them as interest instead of amortizing over the facility term.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Interest capitalization stop dates depend on project completion milestones.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate interest expense and capitalized interest, including verifying capitalization stop dates against project completion records
Inspect the hedge documentation dating and evaluate whether hedge accounting complies with IFRS 9 from inception
Vouch arrangement fees to invoices and recalculate amortization over the facility term
Perform analytical procedures comparing interest expense to average borrowings at effective rates and investigate variances

scenarios.client_context: The group reports two segments, but the media division (which lost money all year) is aggregated into 'industrial' using a new aggregation rationale introduced this year. Goodwill allocated to the media cash-generating unit was not impairment-tested because 'the recoverable amount is obviously above carrying value', per the CFO's memo.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Aggregating a loss-making segment may hide material information required by IFRS 8.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Untested goodwill on a loss-making CGU is a classic impairment risk; the CFO memo is not evidence.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the aggregation rationale against IFRS 8 criteria (similar economic characteristics) and challenge the change
Perform or reperform the impairment test for the media CGU, evaluating cash-flow projections and discount rates
Evaluate segment information in the notes against the internal reports used by the chief operating decision maker
Inspect the CFO's memo and file it as audit evidence that no impairment exists
procedures.trap_explanation: Management's memo is a representation, not evidence — accepting it as audit evidence forgoes testing and creates self-review and bias risk. The impairment test must be independently evaluated.

scenarios.client_context: A small chain with three branches. All sales are cash or card. The bookkeeper reconciles the bank account monthly, but the owner regularly takes cash from the till without recording it.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: Unrecorded cash takings and owner withdrawals mean recorded cash and revenue can both be understated.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Reconciling the account monthly still leaves errors possible in the weeks since the last reconciliation.

procedures.procedure: Obtain a bank confirmation of the closing balance directly from the bank
Perform a proof of cash: reconcile recorded sales and cash bankings per branch for the last month
Review the year-end bank reconciliation and trace outstanding items to the January bank statement

scenarios.client_context: The client records sales directly from its electronic point-of-sale (EPOS) system, which is generally reliable. However, in December the tills were set to 'training mode' for two days during staff onboarding, and those sales never flowed to the accounting system. Refunds are recorded as negative sales.

assertions_high_risk.completeness: The training-mode gap means two days of genuine sales are missing from the ledger.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Refunds recorded as negative sales could conceal fictitious original sales if the original was never real.

procedures.procedure: Reconcile daily EPOS Z-reports to the general ledger for the full year and investigate gaps in December
For a sample of refunds, inspect the refund receipts and original sale records
Compare December sales per square metre with the prior year and with neighbouring months

scenarios.client_context: The client holds bikes and parts in one warehouse behind the shop. A year-end count was performed by the owner and one mechanic. The count sheets were not pre-numbered, and damaged returned bikes awaiting supplier credit were included in the count at full price.

assertions_high_risk.existence: Count sheets without control numbers can be lost or altered — recorded inventory may not exist.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Damaged goods counted at full price overstate inventory; they need NRV write-down.

procedures.procedure: Attend the count, independently test-count a sample of items in both directions, and control the count sheets
Identify the damaged returns area, inspect the goods and evaluate NRV using expected credit notes from suppliers
Trace the final count sheets to the inventory listing and investigate adjustments

scenarios.line_item: Trade receivables with an ageing ledger
scenarios.client_context: The client sells to businesses on 30-day terms. The debtors' ledger is maintained by one clerk, and a single customer (a marketing agency) owes 40% of the balance and is 90 days overdue. The allowance is a flat 2% of total receivables, unchanged for three years.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A flat 2% allowance ignores a concentrated, long-overdue balance; expected credit losses are likely understated.
assertions_high_risk.existence: A single clerk maintaining the ledger without review invites fictitious or misposted balances.

procedures.procedure: Send positive confirmations to the largest customers, including the marketing agency
Test the allowance by comparing expected credit losses per ageing bucket with the flat 2% and recalculating the shortfall
Review cash received after year-end from the agency and trace it to the pre-year-end balance

scenarios.client_context: The client leases cars for consultants and buys laptops and furniture. The fixed asset register was last reconciled to the general ledger 18 months ago, and several fully depreciated assets remain in use. One consultant's lease car was returned mid-year but is still on the register.

assertions_high_risk.existence: The register includes a car that no longer exists; other disposals may be unrecorded too.
assertions_high_risk.accuracy: An 18-month unreconciled register likely disagrees with the ledger.

procedures.procedure: Physically inspect a sample of registered assets and trace assets seen in the office back to the register
Reconcile the fixed asset register to the general ledger and investigate differences
Vouch disposals in the year to lease-return confirmations and sales invoices, and check derecognition and gain/loss

scenarios.client_context: The client prepays its insurance, clinic rent and practice-management software annually. Prepayments are calculated by dividing the invoice by 12 regardless of the period covered. A three-year software licence paid in one invoice in November was treated as fully prepaid at year-end.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Mechanically dividing by 12 misallocates multi-period items; the three-year licence includes two years that are not prepayments of the current period.
assertions_high_risk.cut_off: Invoices straddling year-end need apportionment to the correct period.

procedures.procedure: Vouch each prepayment to the underlying invoice, contract and proof of payment
Recalculate the amortization schedule per invoice based on the actual service period covered
Review payments made after year-end for charges relating to the current period and verify they are not double-counted as prepayments

scenarios.line_item: Deferred income from a government grant
scenarios.client_context: The client received a government grant for hiring and training 50 new technicians, conditioned on keeping them employed for two years. The full grant was recognized in income on receipt in January. Two fired technicians in December may breach the grant conditions, and the grant agreement was never shown to the auditor.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Recognition should follow the pattern of the related costs, not receipt; the condition breach may trigger repayment.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Conditions attached to the grant determine whether the client can keep the money.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Government grants and their conditions require disclosure under IAS 20.

procedures.procedure: Inspect the grant agreement and correspondence with the awarding body, and confirm terms and repayment triggers
Compare the grant income recognition pattern with the qualifying staff costs incurred and recompute deferred income
Review HR records for the two terminated technicians and correspond with the awarding body on the breach
Confirm the grant receipt with the government's bank account
procedures.trap_explanation: Cash receipt is already evidenced by the bank statement — the risky assertions are recognition timing (deferred income) and the attached conditions, which a bank confirmation cannot address.

scenarios.client_context: The client values its 800-head dairy herd at fair value less costs to sell using a herd-model spreadsheet maintained by the farm manager. Milk prices dropped 20% during the year, feed costs rose sharply, and the spreadsheet has not been updated for either. A herd register is kept by ear-tag numbers maintained by the vet.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Fair value under IAS 41 is driven by milk and feed prices; outdated inputs make the valuation stale.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Animals may have been sold or died without the register being updated.

procedures.procedure: Attend a physical headcount and agree to the ear-tag herd register and the valuation schedule
Test the fair value model's inputs (milk price curves, feed costs, cull rates) to current market data and reperform the valuation
Vouch sales of cull cows and calves to livestock market statements

scenarios.client_context: The client owns an office tower measured under the fair value model. The valuation is performed by the client's head of asset management — a qualified surveyor — using a capitalization of net rental income. A major anchor tenant announced departure after year-end (known at authorization date), and the service charge income includes a one-off retro-billing.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A management-prepared fair value, plus a post-year-end tenant departure that changes rental cash flows, creates a high risk the value is overstated.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Whether the valuer is independent, and the valuation technique and inputs, must be disclosed.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the objectivity and competence of the internal valuer and consider obtaining an independent valuer's report for comparison
Test the valuation model inputs: contractual rents, vacancy assumptions, cap rates against market evidence
Inspect the tenant's lease and the departure notice and assess the effect on cash-flow projections and disclosure as a subsequent event
Vouch rental income in the valuation to signed leases and rent statements, excluding the one-off retro-billing

scenarios.client_context: The client's pension scheme actuary produced the year-end valuation using a discount rate set at the beginning of the year. Interest rates rose materially during the year. The client plans a group-wide early retirement programme announced in November, and the triennial actuarial valuation will not be available until three months after the audit report is due.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A stale discount rate plus an announced curtailment (early retirement programme) make the net liability measurement highly sensitive.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Curtailments, scheme characteristics and actuarial assumptions must be disclosed under IAS 19.

procedures.procedure: Engage the auditor's actuarial expert to evaluate the discount rate, mortality and salary assumptions against current market data
Assess the effect of the announced early retirement programme as a curtailment and verify the remeasurement treatment
Agree participant data to the scheme administrator's records
Review the disclosure of assumptions, scheme assets and the sensitivity analysis in the notes

scenarios.client_context: The client imports from Asia in USD and holds USD-denominated payables and bank accounts. The FX rate used at year-end is the rate on the last day the bookkeeper was in the office (three days before year-end). Some USD supplier invoices were recorded at the order-date rate and never retranslated, and a USD loan was inadvertently translated at the wrong functional-currency rate.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Using a non-year-end rate and leaving order-date rates in place are systematic translation errors.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: FX gains/losses on the USD loan may be misstated.

procedures.procedure: Agree the year-end USD/EUR rate used to a reliable published source for the exact reporting date and quantify misstatements
Retranslate a sample of USD payables, bank balances and the loan at the closing rate and reconcile differences
Verify FX gains and losses are presented consistently and disclosed, including the loan's classification
Confirm the USD bank balance with the bank and check it is retranslated at the correct rate

scenarios.client_context: The client is building a custom policy-administration ERP. Costs are capitalized from the start of coding, including routine bug-fixing of the legacy system and general IT staff time booked to the project code. The project manager estimates 70% completion based on 'feel', and go-live is planned next autumn.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Legacy bug fixes and general IT time are expenses, not qualifying development costs — capitalization includes non-eligible items.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Impairment indicators (delays, rising costs) and the completion assessment are judgemental.

procedures.procedure: Review the capitalization policy against IAS 38's six criteria and test a sample of capitalized costs to timesheets and invoices
Assess the measure of completion using objective milestones (module sign-offs, test results) rather than the project manager's estimate
Assess impairment indicators, including budget overruns and timeline slippage
Inspect the board's approval of the ERP project budget
procedures.trap_explanation: Budget approval shows the project was authorized, but provides no evidence about whether individual capitalized costs qualify for capitalization under IAS 38 — the assertion actually at risk.

scenarios.client_context: The utility places surplus funds in savings and two structured deposits whose return depends on an equity index. Interest income is booked from the bank's annual statement received after year-end, and the structured deposit returns were simply estimated at the maximum contingent rate.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Estimated structured-deposit returns at the maximum rate overstate income unless the index condition is actually met.
assertions_high_risk.classification: The contingent return may be a derivative or embedded feature rather than interest income.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate savings interest from deposit certificates and rates, and reconcile to the bank statement
Inspect the structured deposit terms and independently verify the index performance to determine the actual contingent return
Review treasury's deal confirmations and compare booked income to year-end accrued interest schedules for completeness

scenarios.line_item: Other income (disposal gain and scrap sales)
scenarios.client_context: This year other income jumped 300%. It includes a gain on selling a redundant plot of land and steadily growing 'scrap sales' recorded from delivery notes kept in a box in the workshop. The land sale was to the owner's brother-in-law at above-market price.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A related-party land sale at above-market price needs evidence of fair value; the gain may be misstated.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Scrap sales recorded from paper notes may be incomplete.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Amounts may belong in revenue or be one-offs requiring separate presentation.

procedures.procedure: Obtain an independent valuation of the land plot and compare to the sale price, and review related-party disclosure
Perform a completeness check of scrap sales: weighbridge tickets and waste-carrier invoices to recorded income
Vouch the land transfer to the notarial deed, payment and removal from the asset register
Analytically compare scrap income per tonne of input metal purchased

scenarios.client_context: The client's G&A includes travel, IT subscriptions and 'consultancy'. The managing partner's personal travel and his son's 'marketing consultancy' (no deliverables on file) are included in G&A. Expense claims are approved by the claimant themselves in the workflow tool.

assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Self-approval means fictitious or personal expenses can pass into the accounts.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Non-business expenses may be disguised within G&A rather than treated as drawings or related-party transactions.

procedures.procedure: Test a sample of expenses to invoices and business purpose evidence, focusing on travel and consultancy around the partner
Inspect the workflow tool's approval settings and test overrides and self-approvals
Obtain evidence of services actually rendered by the marketing consultancy and assess disclosure as a related-party transaction
Review the completeness of unprocessed invoices by scanning the accounts payable email inbox

scenarios.client_context: The agency holds tenant deposits and landlord rent in segregated client accounts under a regulator's client-money rules. Staff moved EUR 500k from the client account to the office account 'temporarily' during a cash squeeze in December and repaid it in February. The client-account reconciliation is prepared by the accountant who made the transfer.

assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Client money is not the agency's own asset; temporary use of client funds is a regulatory breach and fraud indicator.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Balances due to individual landlords and tenants must be fully recorded.
assertions_high_risk.classification: Client money must be presented separately from the agency's own cash.

procedures.procedure: Test the client-account reconciliation: agree recorded liabilities per landlord and tenant to the client bank balance
Review the client-to-office account transfer, the repayment, and assess disclosure, regulatory reporting and fraud risk
Confirm balances held for a sample of landlords directly with the landlords
Review the segregation of duties over the reconciliation and the transfer authorizations
procedures.trap_explanation: Segregation of duties testing is a controls matter — it doesn't, by itself, verify that the recorded escrow balances exist and are complete. The trap is mistaking control testing for substantive evidence on the balance.

scenarios.line_item: Trading book positions and trading income
scenarios.client_context: The trading desk marks daily positions to fair value using internal models. This year the front-office team overrode model valuations for illiquid credit positions in 40 instances, with approvals recorded in a chat channel instead of the valuation governance log. Desk bonuses are linked to trading P&L.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Front-office overrides on illiquid positions with bonus-linked P&L is a textbook management-bias and fraud risk (ISA 240).
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Fictitious trades or late-recorded cancelled trades could inflate income.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Valuation techniques, model changes and overrides require disclosure.

procedures.procedure: Test the completeness of the valuation override log against chat channels and trade tickets, and evaluate each override's support
Independently price a sample of illiquid positions using broker quotes or alternative models
Confirm open positions and trades with counterparties and the exchange/clearing house
Test cut-off of trades around year-end using settlement data and trade timestamps

scenarios.client_context: The charity receives restricted grants for specific field projects. Grant income is recognized when cash is received, not as project expenditure is incurred. One funder's grant was spent partly on overheads, breaching the agreement, and a new large donation pledged at the year-end gala was recognized in full as income.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: Recognizing restricted grants on receipt rather than matching to eligible expenditure misstates both income and the deferred balance.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: A pledge is not yet income; recognition requires a binding unconditional promise.
assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Restricted vs unrestricted funds must be shown separately in the accounts.

procedures.procedure: Recalculate grant recognition against eligible project expenditure per funding agreements and verify the unspent balance is carried forward as deferred income
Review the gala pledge documentation: is it a binding unconditional promise with collectability assessed?
Trace a sample of project expenditure to funding restrictions and identify breaches, corresponding with the funder where needed

scenarios.client_context: The insurer's outstanding claims reserve relies on case estimates set by claims handlers plus an actuarial IBNR calculation. A new AI claims triage tool was implemented mid-year without parallel running, and average case estimates dropped 15% immediately after go-live. Development factors are based on a five-year history that excludes a period with major hailstorms.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: The 15% drop coinciding with the AI tool suggests systematic underestimation rather than genuine efficiency.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Claims occurred but not yet reported (IBNR) may be understated if history excludes catastrophe patterns.

procedures.procedure: Compare case estimates pre- and post-AI implementation, and re-perform a sample of triage outputs against handler judgement
Use the auditor's actuarial expert to test IBNR development factors including catastrophe-adjusted history
Test claims completeness using the industry claims database and reinsurance bordereaux
Review reserve adequacy and estimation-uncertainty disclosures in the notes

scenarios.client_context: The client grants options to employees with a four-year vesting period and one service condition. This year it modified a struggling division's grants by reducing the vesting period from four years to two 'to retain staff'. The grant-date fair values were computed by the CFO using a Black-Scholes model with a volatility taken from a competitor with a very different profile.

assertions_high_risk.accuracy: The vesting-period modification accelerates expense recognition — the incremental fair value must be recognized.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: A poorly chosen volatility input makes grant-date fair values unreliable.

procedures.procedure: Vouch grants and the modification to board resolutions, option agreements and the cap table
Reperform the Black-Scholes valuation, benchmarking volatility against the client's own traded options history and peer group
Recalculate the expense for the accelerated vesting cohort including the incremental fair value of the modification
Confirm the number of options held per employee directly with the staff
procedures.trap_explanation: Employees' awareness of their option count says nothing about whether the expense is measured correctly under IFRS 2. The audit issue is the model and modification accounting, not confirming holdings with staff.

scenarios.client_context: The lender grew its mortgage book 40% in one year by relaxing income verification for self-employed borrowers — stated income instead of tax returns. Property revaluations for loan-to-value ratios are desktop valuations by an internal team, and early-payment defaults on last year's vintage are already running above tolerance.

assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Stated-income lending plus internal desktop valuations is a classic combination that understates ECL; the rising default rate confirms it.
assertions_high_risk.existence: Rapid growth can mask fraudulent applications; recorded loans may not represent genuine creditworthy borrowers.
assertions_high_risk.rights_and_obligations: Mortgage security must be registered — some registrations may be pending or defective.

procedures.procedure: Test a sample of the new vintage for borrower existence, income evidence and underwriting approval
Independently revalue a sample of collateral using external data and recompute LTVs and ECL staging
Inspect the mortgage security register and confirm registrations for a sample of new loans
Compare early-payment default rates per vintage against management's ECL assumptions and challenge the staging

scenarios.client_context: The bank transfers credit card receivables to securitization vehicles. Management concludes the vehicles are not consolidated because 'the transfer is a true sale'. However, the bank provides a liquidity facility of 40% of the portfolio and a first-loss profit share, and reinvests in the junior tranche. Two new vehicles were set up by the head of the desk using a template from an external law firm, with no legal opinion obtained.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: The liquidity facility, profit share and retained junior tranche indicate the bank retains substantially all the risks — consolidation (IFRS 10) or at least extensive derecognition and disclosure analysis (IFRS 9/IFRS 7) is required.
assertions_high_risk.completeness: Template-based vehicles may never have been through the bank's structured products approval process.

procedures.procedure: Evaluate the consolidation assessment against IFRS 10's power-exposure-to-variable-returns model, including the liquidity facility and retained interests
Test derecognition of the transferred receivables against IFRS 9's pass-of-risk test, and challenge the 'true sale' conclusion without a legal opinion
Review the register of structured entities for completeness and trace the two new vehicles to board approval
Verify the market value of the junior tranche held to trading data
procedures.trap_explanation: Pricing the retained tranche is secondary — the primary question is whether the vehicles should be consolidated at all. A precise valuation of one tranche is meaningless if the whole structure is off-balance-sheet when it shouldn't be.

scenarios.client_context: The treasury desk uses repos for short-term funding. Around quarter-ends, several repos are recorded as outright sales of the bonds with a forward to repurchase — removing them from the balance sheet for a few days. Some counterparties are affiliated funds, and the collateral haircut schedules were not updated after market volatility spiked.

assertions_high_risk.presentation_and_disclosure: Quarter-end 'sales' with repurchase agreements are balance-sheet window dressing — repos must stay on balance sheet under IFRS 9 unless risks genuinely transfer.
assertions_high_risk.valuation_and_allocation: Stale haircut schedules understate collateral calls in a volatile market.
assertions_high_risk.occurrence: Affiliated counterparties raise questions about whether transactions have commercial substance.
